tax.title: Fine-tune tax
tax.lead: Raise or cut any tax. Watch your headroom move.
tax.shortlistLead: Your Director of Tax’s best ideas. Watch your headroom move.

items.name: The basic rate of income tax
items.label: Basic rate

policies.title: Put up the basic rate of income tax

advice.text: Big money; Scotland sets its own rates on wages and pensions.

sources.quote: Scottish Income Tax applies to your wages, pension and most other taxable income.

policies.title: Cut the basic rate of income tax

advice.text: Big money back; Scotland sets its own rates on wages and pensions.

items.name: The higher rate of income tax
items.label: Higher rate

policies.title: Put up the higher rate of income tax

advice.text: Paid by higher earners, a group the freeze keeps growing.

policies.title: Cut the higher rate of income tax

advice.text: Higher earners gain, a group the freeze keeps growing.

items.name: The additional rate of income tax
items.label: Additional rate

policies.title: Put up the additional rate of income tax

advice.text: Raises little: top earners respond strongly to a higher rate.

policies.title: Cut the additional rate of income tax

advice.text: A cut for top earners, who respond strongly to their rate.

policies.title: A new 50% income tax rate above £125,140

advice.text: Symbolic money from the very highest earners.

policies.title: Cut the personal allowance

advice.text: Most taxpayers pay more; some who paid nothing start paying.

policies.title: Raise the personal allowance

advice.text: Most taxpayers gain; people who pay no income tax gain nothing.

policies.title: Lower the higher-rate threshold by 10%

advice.text: Pulls more earners into the higher rate, on top of the freeze.

policies.title: Raise the higher-rate threshold

advice.text: Eases the freeze that pulls more people into the higher rate.

policies.title: End the threshold freeze early

advice.text: Big money back to every taxpayer, from 2028.

policies.title: A child tax allowance for under-fives

advice.text: Starts in 2028; parents who pay no income tax gain nothing.

decisions.title: Tax on dividends, savings and rent

alternatives.name: The rates on dividends, savings and rent

policies.title: Add another 2p to the tax on dividends, savings and rental income

advice.text: Investors pay again, on top of last year’s rise.

policies.title: Undo last year’s rises on dividend, savings and property income

advice.text: Shareholders, savers and landlords keep more of what they earn.

items.name: The main rate of National Insurance
items.label: Main rate

policies.title: Put up National Insurance

advice.text: Big money from every employee and self-employed worker.

policies.title: Cut National Insurance

advice.text: Big money back to every employee and self-employed worker.

policies.title: Put up National Insurance on pay above £50,270

advice.text: Higher earners pay it on every pound above the threshold.

policies.title: Cut National Insurance on pay above £50,270

advice.text: Higher earners gain on every pound above the threshold.

policies.title: Lower the National Insurance threshold

advice.text: Every employee above the threshold pays the same sum more.

policies.title: Raise the National Insurance threshold

advice.text: Every employee above the threshold gains the same sum.

policies.title: Charge full National Insurance on all earnings, however high

advice.text: Big on paper; top earners would find ways to pay less.

policies.title: Charge National Insurance to workers over state pension age

advice.text: Some older workers would cut their hours or stop.

policies.title: Put up National Insurance for the self-employed

advice.text: Self-employed workers pay more on every pound of profit.

policies.title: Cut National Insurance for the self-employed

advice.text: Self-employed workers keep more of every pound of profit.

policies.title: Charge National Insurance on partnership profits

advice.text: Most falls on the best-paid partners; some would restructure.

policies.title: Put up employer National Insurance

advice.text: Firms pay it first; over time it reaches pay and prices.

sources.quote: The OBR judged that the increase in costs to businesses would lead to lower wages and profits.

policies.title: Cut employer National Insurance

advice.text: Firms gain first; over time it reaches pay and prices.

policies.title: Lower the employer National Insurance threshold

advice.text: Firms pay more for every worker; much comes out of pay.

policies.title: Raise the employer National Insurance threshold

advice.text: Firms keep more for every worker; over time it reaches pay.

policies.title: Charge employer National Insurance on pension contributions

advice.text: Big, but employers would cut what they pay in.

policies.title: Put up VAT

advice.text: Big, and felt on every till receipt.

policies.title: Cut VAT

advice.text: Big money; the cut reaches prices only if shops pass it on.

policies.title: Take VAT off gas too

advice.text: Small; every home heated by gas or oil gains.

policies.title: Keep VAT off electricity after March 2027

advice.text: The zero rate ends in March; keeping it holds bills down.

sources.quote: The temporary zero rate applies from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027.

policies.title: Put up the reduced rate of VAT

advice.text: Mostly paid on home heating, so every gas bill goes up.

policies.title: Cut the reduced rate of VAT

advice.text: Mostly paid on home heating, so every gas bill comes down.

policies.title: End the VAT relief on Motability cars

advice.text: Disabled people would pay more to lease a Motability car.

policies.title: Charge 1% VAT on everything now zero-rated

advice.text: A new VAT rate on food and children’s clothes, paid by everyone.

policies.title: Charge VAT on food

advice.text: Big money; food is a bigger share of poorer families’ spending.

policies.title: Charge full VAT on home energy

advice.text: Big money, and it reverses this autumn’s cut on electricity.

policies.title: Charge VAT on public transport fares

advice.text: Big money; bus and train users pay it on every fare.

policies.title: Charge VAT on children’s clothes

advice.text: Parents pay it on every size their children outgrow.

policies.title: Charge VAT on new homes

advice.text: Big money, but buyers of new homes would pay it.

policies.title: Charge VAT on books, newspapers and magazines

advice.text: Readers pay it on every book and newspaper.

items.name: The higher rate of capital gains tax
items.label: Higher rate

policies.title: Put up the higher rate of capital gains tax

advice.text: People can wait to sell; on these figures a rise loses money.

items.name: The lower rate of capital gains tax
items.label: Lower rate

policies.title: Put up the lower rate of capital gains tax

advice.text: Raises next to nothing; the largest rise loses money.

policies.title: Undo the 2024 rise in capital gains tax

advice.text: Sellers of shares and businesses pay less on their gains.

policies.title: Tax fund managers’ carried interest as income

advice.text: Small money from a few thousand fund managers, who can move.

policies.title: Tax capital gains when someone dies

advice.text: Steady money from estates, but nothing before 2028.

policies.title: Charge capital gains tax on people who leave the UK

advice.text: Small, and a handful of people leaving decide what it raises.

policies.title: Charge capital gains tax on main homes

advice.text: Big on paper; homeowners would move less and hold on longer.

policies.title: Put up inheritance tax

advice.text: Paid by more estates each year, as the threshold stays frozen.

policies.title: Cut inheritance tax

advice.text: Families inheriting keep more, and the larger the estate the more.

policies.title: End the extra inheritance tax allowance for family homes

advice.text: Steady money from larger estates passing on a home.

items.label: Undo the 2026 farm and business changes

policies.title: Reverse the 2026 farm and family-business inheritance tax changes

advice.text: Small; farms and family firms go back to full relief.

policies.title: A 1% yearly tax on wealth above £10 million

advice.text: Nothing until 2030-31, and nobody knows how the very rich would respond.

policies.title: A 2% yearly tax on wealth above £10 million

advice.text: Nothing before 2030-31, and hotly contested.

items.label: Double it on bands G and H

policies.title: Double council tax on the biggest homes (bands G and H)

advice.text: Steady money from the biggest homes, in England only.

policies.title: Extend the council tax surcharge to homes over £1.5 million

advice.text: Small money, mostly from homeowners in London and the South East.

policies.title: Put up the 5% band of stamp duty

advice.text: Home buyers pay it on the middle slice; some would move less.

policies.title: Cut the 5% band of stamp duty

advice.text: Home buyers gain on the middle slice of the price.

policies.title: Abolish stamp duty on main homes

advice.text: Expensive; buyers gain, though some of it ends up in prices.

policies.title: Cut the stamp duty surcharge on additional homes back to 3%

advice.text: Small; landlords and second-home buyers pay less stamp duty.

policies.title: Put up corporation tax

advice.text: Steady money from company profits.

policies.title: Cut corporation tax

advice.text: Firms keep more profit; any boost to investment is not counted.

policies.title: Put up business rates

advice.text: Firms in England pay more on their premises.

policies.title: Cut business rates

advice.text: England’s bills only; the other nations set their own.

decisions.title: Tax banks and energy firms more

policies.title: A levy on the interest banks earn at the Bank of England

advice.text: Big only while interest rates stay high; it needs a new law.

policies.title: Double the bank levy

advice.text: Banks would shrink their balance sheets to pay less.

policies.title: Raise the bank surcharge from 3% to 5%

advice.text: Only the largest banks pay, and they choose where profits land.

policies.title: Raise the energy profits levy again, as in 2024

advice.text: Raises less than the first round, and moves with oil prices.

policies.title: Freeze fuel duty in April 2027

advice.text: Small money, felt at every pump; emissions edge up a little.

sources.quote: From 1 April 2027, fuel duty rates will be uprated annually in line with the Retail Price Index.
which will likely maintain any marginal impact of carbon emissions from increased consumption of fossil fuels that this measure may cause

policies.title: Put up fuel duty

advice.text: Drivers pay more on top of planned rises; emissions dip.

policies.title: Cut fuel duty

advice.text: Drivers feel it at the pump; emissions edge up.

policies.title: Put up alcohol duty

advice.text: Paid on every drink, by the alcohol in it.

policies.title: Cut alcohol duty

advice.text: Drinkers and pubs pay less duty on every drink.

policies.title: Put up tobacco duty

advice.text: Small money; smokers pay, and there are fewer each year.

policies.title: Cut tobacco duty by 10%

advice.text: Small money; smokers gain, against the health case for the duty.

policies.title: Put gambling duties up again

advice.text: Betting firms pay again, on top of last year’s rise.

policies.title: Put up car tax

advice.text: Spread across every car and van, whatever it emits.

sources.quote: Rates for second tax payment onwards Petrol or diesel, Electric & Alternative Fuel Single 12 month payment £200

policies.title: Put up air passenger duty

advice.text: Paid on every flight; it barely changes emissions either way.

sources.quote: We expect the measure to have a negligible impact on the environment.

decisions.title: Tax sugar and salt in food

items.label: A new sugar and salt tax

policies.title: A new tax on sugar and salt in food

advice.text: Years to set up, and it shrinks as recipes change.

policies.title: Another push to close the tax gap

advice.text: A repeat of last year’s package; nobody has costed a further round.

spending.title: Fine-tune spending
spending.lead: Trim or top up any budget. A top-up costs what a trim saves.
spending.shortlistLead: Your Director of Public Spending’s best ideas. A top-up costs what a trim saves.

notes.text: Departments’ day-to-day budgets are set to 2028-29. Cutting one reopens a minister’s deal.
After that, the forecast already has the budgets it does not protect falling 4.4% a year after inflation.
Most public services here are England’s budgets. The other nations get a share through their own grants (the Barnett formula), which our prices leave out.

sources.note: Annex B.13, comparability factors at Spending Review 2025

policies.title: Cut health and social care

advice.text: Protected, and the biggest budget. A cut shows up in waiting lists.

policies.title: Spend more on health and social care

advice.text: Waiting lists fall slowly; strikes and pay awards are the risks.

policies.title: Cut schools and education

advice.text: Protected. Special needs costs already squeeze what schools get.

policies.title: Spend more on schools and education

advice.text: Special needs demand keeps rising and would take much of it.

policies.title: Cut defence, day to day

advice.text: Any cut puts the defence promise at risk.

policies.title: Spend more on defence, day to day

advice.text: Pays people and keeps kit running. It buys no submarines.

policies.title: Cut the Home Office and borders

advice.text: The plan assumes asylum costs fall; if not, it overspends.

policies.title: Spend more on the Home Office and borders

advice.text: Asylum costs are eating a budget that is already falling.

policies.title: Cut prisons and courts

advice.text: Small money, and ministers have promised not to shorten sentences.

policies.title: Spend more on prisons and courts

advice.text: Buys staff and repairs, not new cells yet.

policies.title: Cut grants to councils

advice.text: Small money here; councils would feel it in social care.

policies.title: Raise grants to councils

advice.text: Councils would feel it first in adult social care.

policies.title: Cut transport, day to day

advice.text: Small money. Already falling in real terms, and unprotected.

policies.title: Spend more on transport, day to day

advice.text: Small money; it pays for bus and rail subsidies.

policies.title: Cut the Foreign Office and aid

advice.text: Small money. Aid is already falling, and unprotected.

policies.title: Spend more on the Foreign Office and aid

advice.text: Small money, and it softens the cut to aid.

policies.title: Cut all other departments

advice.text: Mostly Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland’s grants; also energy and net zero.

policies.title: Spend more on all other departments

advice.text: Most of it would reach Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

policies.title: Free school meals for every child

advice.text: England only. It pays for every place, not just meals eaten.

policies.title: Keep the £2 bus fare cap running

advice.text: Small, and only for buses in England outside London.

policies.title: An AI retraining programme

advice.text: A sum set aside; whether it works depends on delivery.

policies.title: Cut public investment

advice.text: Counts against the debt rule, not the day-to-day rule.

policies.title: Spend more on public investment

advice.text: Counts against the debt rule only, and departments often underspend.

policies.title: More council and social rent homes

advice.text: Counts against the debt rule only; the homes arrive over a decade.

policies.title: Fund the defence plan’s gap

advice.text: The defence plan counts on this money, and nothing funds it yet.

policies.title: Defence at 3% of GDP now, not in 2030-31

advice.text: Costs most at first; the bill fades by 2030.

policies.title: Cut pensioner benefits

advice.text: Mostly the state pension. A cut reaches every pensioner.

policies.title: Raise pensioner benefits

advice.text: Mostly the state pension, which the triple lock already raises.

items.label: Prices only, ending the triple lock

policies.title: Link the state pension to prices only, ending the triple lock

advice.text: Every pensioner feels it, and the gap widens each year.

items.label: An earnings link, ending the triple lock

policies.title: Replace the pension triple lock with an earnings link

advice.text: Small now and growing; pensions still rise with pay over time.

policies.title: Cut universal credit

advice.text: Inside the welfare cap: already above it, but within its margin.

policies.title: Raise universal credit

advice.text: Reaches the poorest families first, and pushes further over the welfare cap.

policies.title: Cut other benefits

advice.text: Carers and housing support; Northern Ireland sets most of its own.

policies.title: Raise other benefits

advice.text: Reaches carers and housing support; Scotland pays carers its own benefit.

policies.title: A protected floor in Universal Credit

advice.text: Small, and it reaches the poorest households first.

policies.title: Raise housing benefit to match local rents

advice.text: Renters feel it, though some of it ends up with landlords.

items.label: Limit unemployment insurance to six months

policies.title: Time-limit the new unemployment insurance to six months

advice.text: Saves nothing until 2030-31, then the same each year.

policies.title: Cut disability benefits

advice.text: Caseloads are rising fast, and past cuts saved less than planned.

policies.title: Raise disability benefits

advice.text: Rising caseloads already push this line up fast without it.

items.label: Stop them for milder mental health conditions

policies.title: Stop disability benefits for milder mental health conditions

advice.text: Big on paper; past disability reforms saved less than planned.

items.label: Go ahead with the 2025 PIP cuts

policies.title: Go ahead with the 2025 cuts to PIP

advice.text: Undoes last year’s U-turn; your own MPs will fight it.

policies.title: Assess children in person for Disability Living Allowance

advice.text: Nothing until 2030-31; some new autism and ADHD claims would fail.

policies.title: Cancel the extra efficiency savings planned from 2028

advice.text: The OBR already doubts these savings will ever come.

policies.title: Reinstate the two-child limit

advice.text: Families on benefits pay, and it breaks a promise.

items.label: Winter fuel for pension credit only

policies.title: Limit winter fuel payments to pensioners on pension credit

advice.text: Brings back a cut the government reversed last year.

items.label: Let the student loan threshold rise

policies.title: Let the student loan repayment threshold rise again

advice.text: Small money; graduates in England and Wales keep a little more.
